2-In: Brings a stereo pair into the patch from audio inputs 1/2 or 3/4, or from bus 1/2 or 3/4 (Source). Pad sets the input gain.
2-Out: Sends a stereo pair out of the patch: to outputs 1/2 or 3/4, to FX 1/2 or 3/4 for the FX area, or to bus 1/2 or 3/4 (Dest). Pad adds up to +18 dB of gain.
4-In: Brings four mono signals into the patch, from the four audio inputs or the four buses (Source). Pad sets the input gain.
4-Out: Sends four mono signals out of the patch: to the four audio outputs, to the FX area or to the buses (Dest). Pad adds up to +18 dB of gain.
8Counter: Logic counter with eight outputs: each pulse on Clk moves a single high output one step along, from Out1 to Out8 and round again. Rst resets it. Useful for short step patterns and for switching between eight destinations.
ADConv: 8-bit analog-to-digital converter: turns the input level into an 8-bit two's-complement number on eight logic outputs, D0 to D7. Combine it with DAConv and logic modules for bit-crushing and other digital tricks.
Automate: Sends a MIDI controller (Control, Channel) from the patch and also follows that controller when it arrives at MIDI in, so the value stays in step with the other device. Used to store and recall an external instrument's settings in a patch.
BinCounter: 8-bit binary counter: each Clk pulse adds one, and the eight logic outputs (weights 1, 2, 4 ... 128) show the count in binary. Rst sets it back to zero. Each output divides the clock by a further power of two.
Blue2Red: Internal module that cannot be placed in a patch: carries a control signal on as an audio-rate signal.
Clip: Clips the signal at an adjustable level (Clip, with a modulation input), on both sides (Sym) or asymmetrically (Asym). Gives hard distortion on audio, or limits the range of a control signal.
ClkDiv: Clock divider: outputs one pulse for every n pulses on Clk (Divider, up to 128). In the gated mode the output pulses keep the width of the input pulses; in the toggled mode the output changes state each time, giving a square wave. Reset restarts the count.
ClkGen: Clock source: logic pulses on every 16th and every 96th note at its own Tempo (with Swing), or following the master clock (Source). Also outputs ClkActive and a Sync pulse at a selectable interval. Drives sequencers and other clocked modules.
CompLev: Compares the input with the Level value: the logic output is high while the input is at or above the level, and low otherwise. Turns a control or audio signal into a gate.
CompSig: Compares two signals: the logic output is high while A is at or above B, and low otherwise. Turns the crossings of two signals into gates and triggers.
Compress: Stereo compressor: lowers the level of signals above Thres by Ratio, with Attack and Release times and an Output level. With SideChn on, the SideChain input controls the gain reduction. Evens out dynamics and adds punch.
ConstSwM: Push button that outputs the set Value while it is held and zero otherwise, bipolar or unipolar (Pol). Assigned to a panel button, it gives a manual burst of modulation.
ConstSwT: On/off button that outputs the set Value while it is on and zero while it is off, bipolar or unipolar (Pol). Assigned to a panel button, it switches an offset or a modulation in and out.
Constant: Outputs a fixed control value set with the knob, bipolar or unipolar (Pol). A general-purpose knob for driving any modulation input, or a fixed offset.
CtrlRcv: Receives a MIDI controller (Control, Channel): Val follows its value and Rcv pulses on each message. Lets an external MIDI controller or sequencer drive anything in the patch.
CtrlSend: Sends a MIDI controller message (Control, Channel) with the Value knob plus the Value input, each time the Send input goes high; the Send output then pulses, for chaining with PCSend. Controls other MIDI devices from the patch.
DAConv: 8-bit digital-to-analog converter: reads an 8-bit two's-complement number on its eight logic inputs, D0 to D7, and outputs the matching bipolar level. The counterpart of ADConv.
DXRouter: Connects six Operator modules in one of the 32 DX7 algorithms (Algortm), with operator feedback (FeedBk). The operators' outputs go to its inputs and its outputs back to their FM inputs; Main carries the mix of the carriers.
Delay: Delays the edges of a logic signal by the set Time (with a modulation input and three ranges): the rising edge, the falling edge or both, depending on the mode. Lengthens, shortens or offsets gates and triggers.
DelayA: Mono echo with delay Time (free or clock-synced), feedback (FB), a lowpass filter (Flt LP) and a Dry/Wet mix.
DelayB: Mono echo with delay Time (free or clock-synced), feedback (FB), lowpass and highpass filters and a Dry/Wet mix, with inputs to modulate the feedback and the mix.
DelayDual: Two delay taps on one input, each with its own Time and Time modulation input. The maximum time depends on the selected range.
DelayQuad: Four delay taps on one input, each with its own Time and modulation input; OutMain gives the longest delay of the selected range. Times can follow the clock (Time Md). For multi-tap echoes and rhythmic delays.
Device: Brings the synth's performance controls into the patch: mod wheel, aftertouch, control and sustain pedals, pitch stick and the two global wheels.
Digitizer: Lowers the sample rate (Rate, with a modulation input) and the bit depth (Bits) of a signal, for lo-fi grit and aliasing.
DlyClock: Delays a signal by a number of clock steps rather than by time: each value sampled from the input comes out the set number of Clk pulses later (Delay). Shifts a sequence or melody by whole steps.
DlyEight: Delay line with eight evenly spaced taps: each output is one more step of Time later than the one before. For multi-tap echoes, comb effects and rhythmic patterns.
DlyShiftReg: Eight-stage shift register: on each Clk pulse the input is sampled to Out1 and the earlier values move one output along. Derives canons and harmonies from a single note sequence.
DlySingleA: Plain delay line with a fixed Time and no modulation, within the selected range.
DlySingleB: Plain delay line with a Time knob and a Time modulation input, within the selected range. Short modulated delays give chorus, flanging and vibrato.
DlyStereo: Stereo echo from a mono input, with separate left and right Time, feedback (FB) and cross-feedback (X-FB), lowpass and highpass filters and a Dry/Wet mix. Times can follow the clock.
Driver: Internal module that cannot be placed in a patch; its Embouch and Stiffn controls suggest the exciter of a physical model.
DrumSynth: Analog-style drum voice: two tuned oscillators (master and slave) with pitch bend, a click and filtered noise, each with its own decay. Played by Trig, with Vel and Pitch inputs. Covers kicks, snares, toms, hats and other percussion.
EnvADDSR: Envelope with an extra breakpoint: Attack, Decay 1 to Break 1, Decay 2 to Break 2, then Release. The sustain holds at the first or second break level (SusPlac). For contours more detailed than an ADSR.
EnvADR: Attack-Decay or Attack-Release envelope (Type), started by a trigger or held by a gate (Trigged). End goes high when the envelope finishes, to start another envelope or to loop this one. Built-in VCA (In/Out).
EnvADSR: Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release envelope held by a Gate. Env is the control output; the built-in VCA applies the envelope to In at Out, and AM scales its level. The usual choice for amplitude and filter contours.
EnvAHD: Attack, Hold and Decay envelope started by a pulse on Trig: it rises, stays at full level for the Hold time, then falls. Suits percussive sounds and timed gating. Built-in VCA (In/Out).
EnvD: Decay-only envelope: jumps to full level on a Trig pulse, then falls over the Decay time. Built-in VCA (In/Out) and an AM input. For clicks, plucks and short modulation.
EnvFollow: Follows the loudness of an audio signal and outputs it as a control signal, smoothed by Attack and Release. Lets one sound control another: auto-wah, ducking, dynamic filtering.
EnvH: Hold envelope: on a Trig pulse the output goes to full level for the HldTime, then drops to zero. A timed gate, with a built-in VCA (In/Out).
EnvMulti: Envelope with four Time and Level pairs and a selectable sustain point (L1, L2 or L3, or Trg for none). For contours that an ADSR cannot draw. Built-in VCA (In/Out).
Eq2Band: Bass and treble shelving EQ: Lo Gain at 80, 110 or 160 Hz, Hi Gain at 6, 8 or 12 kHz, and an output Level.
Eq3band: Three-band EQ: bass and treble shelves with selectable corner frequencies, a mid band with adjustable frequency (Mid Frq), and an output Level.
EqPeak: Parametric peak EQ: boosts or cuts (Gain) a band around Freq, with adjustable bandwidth (BWidth). Shapes the tone or picks out a resonance.
Fade1-2: Sends one input to two outputs in a variable balance, set by the knob and the Mod input. For moving a signal between two destinations.
Fade2-1: Fades between two inputs into one output, set by the knob and the Mod input. For blending two sources or two modulations.
Flanger: Flanger effect: a short, swept delay with feedback, for the familiar jet-like whoosh. Rate sets the sweep speed, Range the span of the sweep and FB its intensity.
FlipFlop: Logic flip-flop with Q and inverted (NotQ) outputs, working as a D-type or a set-reset flip-flop (mode). Res clears it. For latching events and dividing clocks by two.
FltClassic: Resonant lowpass filter in the style of classic analog synths, with a 12, 18 or 24 dB/oct slope, keyboard tracking (KBT) and two pitch modulation inputs.
FltComb: Comb filter: a short delay tuned to Freq with feedback (FB), giving notches or peaks across the harmonic series (Type). Tracks the keyboard and takes pitch and feedback modulation. For flanging, metallic and plucked tones.
FltHP: Highpass filter without resonance, with a 6 to 36 dB/oct slope (mode), keyboard tracking and a Freq modulation input. Removes low frequencies cleanly.
FltLP: Lowpass filter without resonance, with a 6 to 36 dB/oct slope (mode), keyboard tracking and a Freq modulation input. Smooths and darkens signals.
FltMulti: Resonant multimode filter with lowpass, bandpass and highpass outputs available at once, a 6 or 12 dB/oct slope, keyboard tracking and pitch modulation inputs.
FltNord: Resonant filter with lowpass, bandpass, highpass and band-reject types, a 12 or 24 dB/oct slope, keyboard tracking, and inputs for pitch, linear frequency and resonance modulation.
FltPhase: Phaser filter: a chain of allpass stages giving notches or peaks. Notch sets how many, Spread their spacing and FB the feedback, the last two with modulation inputs; tracks the keyboard. Modulating Freq gives phasing sweeps.
FltStatic: Resonant filter, lowpass, bandpass or highpass, with fixed settings and no modulation inputs. For static tone shaping.
FltVoice: Formant filter that imitates vowels: Nav (and the Vowel input) moves between three chosen vowels, Vowel 1 to 3, with frequency shift and resonance. For talking and singing timbres.
FreqShift: Frequency shifter: moves every partial of the signal by the same number of hertz, giving the shifted-up (Up) and shifted-down (Dn) results at once. Gives inharmonic, metallic and slowly phasing effects.
Fx-In: FX-area input: receives what the voice area sends to FX 1/2 or 3/4. All voices arrive mixed together, so it gets louder as more notes play. Pad sets the gain.
Gate: Two logic gates, each combining two logic inputs with a selectable function: AND, NAND, OR, NOR, XOR or XNOR. For combining gates and triggers.
Glide: Slews a control signal so that jumps become glides, as in portamento: Time sets the speed and Shape the log or linear curve. The Active button and the On input switch it on.
Invert: Two logic inverters: each output is high when its input is low, and low when it is high.
KeyQuant: Scales the input by Range, then rounds it to a note of the scale picked on the mini keyboard, either the closest one or spread evenly over the range (Capture). Keeps random or continuous signals in key.
Keyboard: Per-voice keyboard signals from the G2's keys or MIDI in: Pitch, Gate, attack velocity (Lin and Exp), Release velocity and the bare Note value (without bend or glide). The usual source of an oscillator's pitch and an envelope's gate.
LevAdd: Adds a positive or negative offset to a signal (Offset, bipolar or unipolar). Shifts a modulation range or centres a signal.
LevAmp: Amplifies or attenuates a signal by Gain, on a linear or dB scale (Type). For scaling modulation amounts or boosting quiet signals.
LevConv: Converts the range of a signal: set what the input is (bipolar, positive or negative: InType) and choose the output range and inversion (OutType). For example, turns a bipolar LFO into a positive-only one.
LevMod: Amplitude and ring modulator: the Depth knob goes from no effect, through amplitude modulation, to full ring modulation of In by Mod. The ModDepth input modulates that amount. Works on audio and control signals.
LevMult: Multiplies its two inputs, like a VCA: In is scaled by Mod. The basic way to control a level with an envelope or LFO.
LevScaler: Keyboard level scaling: changes the signal's level (and a Level output) with separate gains below and above a breakpoint note (L.Gain, BrkPnt, R.Gain), following the keyboard (KBT) or the Note input.
LfoA: LFO with six waveforms (sine, triangle, saw, square and two random), rate modulation and keyboard tracking, over several rate ranges including tempo sync. Poly gives each voice its own LFO, Mono one for all.
LfoB: LFO with a choice of basic waveforms, adjustable and modulatable phase, rate modulation, keyboard tracking, a reset input (Rst) and a Sync output.
LfoC: Compact LFO whose waveform is set in the editor rather than by a live control, which uses less of the synth's processing. Rate modulation and the usual rate ranges, including tempo sync.
LfoShpA: LFO with six waveforms whose Shape and Phase can be set and modulated, rate modulation and keyboard tracking. Also has reset (Rst) and direction (Dir) inputs and a Snc output.
MetNoise: Metallic noise source with an inharmonic, clangy timbre, adjustable by Color and Freq, each with a modulation input. For cymbals, hi-hats and bell-like sounds.
MinMax: Outputs the lower of its two inputs on Min and the higher on Max. For combining modulation sources or limiting one signal by another.
Mix1-1A: One-channel level control with an on/off button and a chain input for joining other mixers. Lin/Exp sets the knob's curve.
Mix1-1S: Stereo one-channel level control: one Level and on/off button for a stereo pair, with stereo chain inputs.
Mix2-1A: Two-input mixer with a level knob and on/off button per input, and a chain input.
Mix2-1B: Two-input mixer with a level knob and an Inv (invert) button per input, and a chain input. Useful for adding or subtracting control signals.
Mix4-1A: Sums four inputs to one output, with no controls.
Mix4-1B: Four-input mixer with a level knob per input and a chain input.
Mix4-1C: Four-input mixer with a level knob and on/off button per input, a -6 dB pad and a chain input.
Mix4-1S: Stereo mixer for four stereo pairs, with a level knob and on/off button per pair and stereo chain inputs.
Mix8-1A: Sums eight inputs to one output with no level controls; Pad lowers the sum by 6 or 12 dB.
Mix8-1B: Eight-input mixer with a level knob per input, a 0, -6 or -12 dB pad and a chain input.
MixFader: Eight-channel mixer laid out like a mixing desk, with a fader and on/off button per channel, a pad and a chain input.
MixStereo: Six-channel stereo mixer: a level and a pan control per input, and a Master level. Places mono sources in a stereo image.
ModADSR: ADSR envelope whose Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release can each be modulated from a control input, with amounts set by knobs. Built-in VCA (In/Out). For example, shorter decays on higher notes.
ModAHD: Attack, Hold and Decay envelope with control inputs to modulate each of the three times. Built-in VCA (In/Out).
ModAmt: Sets how much a modulation signal affects another signal: In is scaled by Mod according to Amount, on a linear or exponential curve. In the 1-m mode, In passes unchanged when Amount is at its minimum.
MonoKey: Monophonic keyboard: a single Pitch, Gate and Vel for the whole patch, with last, low or high note priority (Priorty), as on classic mono synths.
Mux1-8: Sends its input to one of eight outputs, chosen by the value at Ctrl. Routes a signal to different places under modulation or sequencer control.
Mux8-1: Picks one of eight inputs by the value at Ctrl. Lets a sequencer, an LFO or the voice number choose among sources.
Mux8-1X: Picks one of eight inputs by the value at Ctrl, with an adjustable crossfade between neighbouring inputs (X-Fade) for smooth changes. For scanning through sounds or waveforms.
Noise: Noise source, from bright white noise to darker coloured noise (Color). For wind, breath, percussion and random modulation.
NoiseGate: Mutes a signal while it is below Thresh, opening and closing with the set Attack and Release times; Env follows the input's level as a control signal. Removes hiss and hum between notes.
NoteDet: Watches for one note (Note) from the keyboard or MIDI: outputs a Gate while it is held, with its attack (Vel) and release (RelVel) velocities. Lets a single key trigger events in the patch.
NoteQuant: Scales the input by Range, then rounds it to steps of a set number of semitones (Notes). Turns smooth control signals into note values.
NoteRcv: Detects one MIDI note (Note, Channel): outputs a Gate while it is held, with its attack (Vel) and release (RelVel) velocities. Triggers patch events from a MIDI keyboard or sequencer.
NoteScaler: Scales a control signal in semitone units: Range sets how far the output can move. Sets how many notes a modulation, controller or sequence spans.
NoteSend: Sends MIDI notes from the patch on a set channel: Gate starts and ends each note, and Note and Vel set its number and velocity, from the knobs or the inputs.
NoteZone: Passes incoming MIDI notes within a range (NoteMin to NoteMax) from one channel to another channel or slot, transposed if wanted, with or without controllers (Filter). For splits and layers.
Operator: DX7-style FM operator: a sine oscillator with its own four-rate, four-level envelope, keyboard level and rate scaling, velocity sensitivity and amplitude modulation. Six of them with DXRouter make a DX voice.
OscA: The basic oscillator: sine, triangle, saw, or a square at 50, 25 or 10% pulse width (Wave), with keyboard tracking and Pitch and PitchVar modulation inputs.
OscB: Oscillator with sine, triangle, saw, square and DualSaw waves, a modulatable Shape (pulse width), an FM input and hard sync. A flexible source for subtractive sounds.
OscC: Oscillator with OscA's waveforms, the waveform being set in the editor rather than by a live control to save processing. Has pitch modulation, an FM input and hard sync.
OscD: Light oscillator with the waveform set in the editor and a single Pitch input: no FM, sync or pitch modulation knob.
OscDual: Oscillator mixing three waveforms with their own levels: a square with adjustable width (Sqr PW), a saw with phase offset, and a sub-octave square. Inputs for sync, pulse width and phase modulation.
OscMaster: Makes no sound: outputs a pitch control signal (Coarse, Fine, keyboard tracking, modulation) to tune the Pitch inputs of several oscillators or filters together.
OscNoise: Noise in a band around the set pitch: a narrow Width gives a pitched, breathy tone, a wide one broad noise. Tracks the keyboard; for flute, wind and whistling sounds.
OscPM: Oscillator with a phase modulation input (Phase M), the technique behind DX-style FM. The waveform is set in the editor; has pitch modulation and hard sync.
OscPerc: Percussive oscillator: each pulse on Trig starts a decaying tone, shaped by Decay, Click and Punch. For toms, kicks, bells and other struck sounds.
OscShpA: Oscillator with six waveforms (four sine variants, TriSaw and Pulse) whose Shape can be set and modulated, plus FM and hard sync. Moving the shape gives evolving timbres.
OscShpB: Oscillator with shapable waveforms like OscShpA's, the waveform being set in the editor. Shape modulation, FM and hard sync.
OscString: Plucked-string model: a short audio burst on In excites a string tuned to the set pitch, with Decay and Damp setting the ring time and brightness. Feed it a noise burst for guitar, harp and similar sounds.
Overdrive: Overdrive distortion: Drive (with a modulation input) pushes the signal into warm saturation, with four characters (Type) and symmetric or asymmetric shaping (Shape).
PCSend: Sends a MIDI program change (Program, Channel) each time the Send input goes high. Selects sounds on other MIDI instruments from the patch.
PShift: Pitch shifter: transposes a signal up or down (Coarse, Fine, with a Pitch modulation input) while keeping its harmonics in tune. Delay sets the length of the internal delay line.
Pan: Places a mono signal in the stereo field with Pan and a modulation input, on a log or linear law.
PartQuant: Rounds a pitch control signal to the harmonic series, so an oscillator moves only by overtone intervals of its base note (within Range). For natural-trumpet and harmonic sweep effects.
Phaser: Phaser effect with two characters (Type I and Type II), the speed of the sweep (Rate) and feedback (FB).
PitchTrack: Finds the pitch of a single-note audio input and outputs it as a Pitch control signal, with a Gate while a pitch is found and a Period pulse. Thresh sets the minimum input level. Lets a voice or instrument play the patch.
Pulse: Outputs a logic pulse of a set length (Time, with a modulation input and three ranges) on the rising or falling edge of its input (mode). Turns gates into triggers, or lengthens short triggers.
RandomA: Random LFO: new random values at the set Rate, from stepped (Edge 100%) to smoothly gliding (Edge 0%). Step sets how far each new value can move.
RandomB: Random LFO with rate modulation and keyboard tracking: new random values at the set Rate, with Step setting how far each value can move and Edge how smoothly it gets there.
Red2Blue: Internal module that cannot be placed in a patch: carries an audio-rate signal on as a control signal.
Rect: Rectifier: keeps only the positive or the negative half of a signal, or folds all of it to one polarity (full wave). Raises audio by an octave, or makes a bipolar LFO unipolar.
Resonator: Internal module that cannot be placed in a patch: a tuned string or tube resonator for physical modelling.
Reverb: Stereo reverb with a choice of room types, decay Time, brightness (Bright) and a Mix knob balancing the direct and reverberated sound.
RndClkA: Outputs a new random value at each pulse on Clk; the Dice button draws one by hand. Step sets how far each value can move. For random notes and modulation in time with a clock.
RndClkB: Outputs a new random value at each pulse on Clk, with a modulatable Step. Rst jumps to the point of the pseudo-random sequence chosen by Seed, so a random pattern can be repeated.
RndPattern: Plays repeating random patterns, stepped by Clk: Pattern and Bank (plus the A and B inputs) choose the pattern and Loop its length. Outputs stepped values or random pulses (mode). Reproducible random sequences.
RndTrig: At each pulse on Clk, decides at random whether to pass it to the output, with a modulatable probability (Prob). For random rhythmic variation.
S&H: Sample & hold: on each rising edge at Ctrl, captures the input value and holds it until the next. Fed with noise, it gives the classic stepped random modulation.
Saturate: Soft saturation with four curves: rounds off the signal's peaks, with the depth set by Sat and its modulation input. Adds warmth or gentle compression.
Scratch: Varispeed effect that imitates a tape or a record pushed back and forth: P Ratio (and its modulation input) sets the playback speed and direction.
SeqCtr: 16-step sequencer whose current step is chosen by the value at Ctrl rather than by a clock; Val and Trig output that step's value and event. Optional crossfade between steps (XFade).
SeqEvent: 16-step trigger sequencer with two rows of steps and an output for each (Trig1, Trig2). Stepped by Clk; Link chains sequencers. For drum and percussion patterns.
SeqLev: 16-step sequencer of control levels, bipolar or unipolar, with a row of event steps for triggers or gates. Stepped by Clk; Link chains sequencers. For modulation patterns.
SeqNote: 16-step note sequencer: each step holds a note, with a row of event steps for triggers or gates, adjustable length and inputs for recording. Stepped by Clk; Link chains sequencers.
SeqVal: 16-step sequencer of values shown as numbers, bipolar or unipolar, with a row of event steps for triggers or gates. Stepped by Clk; Link chains sequencers.
ShpExp: Exponential waveshaper: bends the signal with a power curve (x2 to x5), by an amount set with Shape and its modulation input. Adds harmonics to audio or reshapes control signals.
ShpStatic: Fixed waveshaper with four curves (x2, x3 and their inverses). Adds harmonics to audio or changes the response of a control signal.
StChorus: Stereo chorus: thickens a mono input into a wide stereo signal with detuned copies. Detune sets how far apart they drift, Amount how much of the effect is heard.
Status: Patch status signals: PatchActive goes high once the patch is loaded or activated, VarActive drops briefly when the variation changes, and VoiceNo gives each voice its own value. For start-up actions and per-voice differences.
Sw1-2: Sends its input to one of two outputs, chosen with buttons (Dest). Ctrl outputs the choice as a value that the Mux modules' Ctrl inputs follow.
Sw1-2M: Momentary switch: the input goes to OutOn while the button is held, and to OutOff otherwise.
Sw1-4: Sends its input to one of four outputs, chosen with buttons (Dest). Ctrl outputs the choice as a value that the Mux modules' Ctrl inputs follow.
Sw1-8: Sends its input to one of eight outputs, chosen with buttons (Dest). Ctrl outputs the choice as a value that the Mux modules' Ctrl inputs follow.
Sw2-1: Picks one of two inputs with buttons (Source): a simple A/B switch. Ctrl outputs the choice as a value that the Mux modules' Ctrl inputs follow.
Sw2-1M: Momentary switch: outputs InOn while the button is held, and InOff otherwise.
Sw4-1: Picks one of four inputs with buttons (Source). Ctrl outputs the choice as a value that the Mux modules' Ctrl inputs follow.
Sw8-1: Picks one of eight inputs with buttons (Source). Ctrl outputs the choice as a value that the Mux modules' Ctrl inputs follow.
SwOnOffM: Momentary on/off switch: passes the input only while the button is held. Assigned to a panel button, it gives a manual trigger or gate.
SwOnOffT: Latching on/off switch: passes or mutes the input. Assigned to a panel button, it switches parts of a patch in or out.
T&H: Track & hold: the output follows the input while Ctrl is high, and keeps the last value while it is low.
ValSw1-2: Sends its input to OutOn while the value at Ctrl is at or above the set Value, and to OutOff below it.
ValSw2-1: Switches its output between two inputs when the value at Ctrl crosses the set Value.
Vocoder: 16-band vocoder: imposes the changing spectrum of the Ctrl signal, such as a voice, on the In signal, such as a synth. Each analysis band can be sent to a different synthesis band for spectral effects.
WahWah: Wah-wah filter: a peaked filter swept by Sweep and its input. For the talking guitar sound, or an auto-wah driven by an envelope or LFO.
WaveWrap: Wave wrapper: as the gain rises (WrpGain, with a modulation input) the signal folds back on itself instead of clipping, adding bright, complex harmonics.
WindSw: Window switch: passes the input, and sets Gate high, while the value at Ctrl lies between From and To. Acts on one zone of a controller or of the keyboard.
X-Fade: Crossfades between In1 and In2 with the XFade knob and the Mod input, on a log or linear law. For morphing between two sounds or two modulations.
ZeroCnt: Estimates the pitch of an audio input by counting its zero crossings, and outputs it as a control signal. Works best on simple waveforms with few harmonics.
